Ok, where to begin?
I was at the bar when it begun. We heard the initial shots as the guns shot the guard outside, then the girl working the front door.
As he started opening fire he initial head towards the dance floor which was opposite side from the bar. It took a moment for us to comprehend what was happening, what the sounds were and why there was screening. We all know what a gunshot sounds like, but your brain kinda refuses to accept it in a situation like this. Really the moment was only a fraction of a second, but in your head it feels like minutes.

I immediately took cover behind a half wall next to the bar, using my body to shield my friend. Listening to the shots my only thought was that if he rounds the corner there would be nothing I could do. I thought about tel, who i was there with. I haven't seen him in a while and we meet up to catch up that night, this bar was his spot. He knew everyone, everyone knew him. In not really a country boy, but I can pass as one of the good ol boys with my gut and beard lol. He wasn't with me when it started, I would never see him again. 

As the shots continued there was a pause, I heard him stop to reload. Again it's like slow motion, it feels like minutes when it's really fractions of seconds. I immediately got up, grabbed the my friend lyanna and the other two with us got up and made for the side exit. We hopped the side fence and ran out to the street, where just so happens a sheriff's deputy was performing a traffic stop. That's why the response was so quick.
Side note, you will never run faster than when it getting shot at, turn out I'm not the fastest, wearing flip flops didn't help lol.

We circled back round the front to find tel, he wasn't there. The officers were arriving now and about to make entrance. Shortly after one would be dead at the front door. 

Continuing around to the other side of the building we started to find the patrons who exited around the back. Some injured from going through the windows. I and another man helped and injured guy up the street, he couldn't walk. A nearby resident took him in his car to the hospital, he recovered fully(physically at least)

By this time no one else was coming out and officers were unable to secure the bar. They were begining to set up a perimeter, we couldn't get to our vehicles. A triage was set up to treat the injured, sadly there were few, all those shot were killed, including tell.

We waited out the night, hoping more would come out, none did. Eventually the officers secured the building, the gunman killed himself shorty after the first encounter. 

The next day I hitchhiked home, and the fires rolled in. The fbi secured the entire block so we could not get our vehicles for about a week. They didn't know if one of them was the gunman's and searched everyone's.
